title: The ratzon kadum in circles and in straightness: a will for Himself that holds every detail
overview:
Chapter 17 opens the details of the *Kav*, in circles and in *yosher*, by explaining the *ratzon kadum*. It is the simple will already decided in the Essence, come up in a thought. Its letters are a copy, no longer the Essence's own, yet its content is the same, and it is still a will for Himself: for His own sitting, not for the chair. Knowing Himself, He knows every detail, the way someone who knows a man knows his house. So every creature, a bug, a squirrel, a drunk in the street, is a detail of the King and deserves respect, and the finished house, the end of the seventh millennium, came up first.

The *Zohar* calls it *Atika d'Atikin* and *Atika Stima'a*; it is revealed in the *metzach* of *Atika Kadisha*, *Atik* and *Arich* of *Atzilus*. In the circles each lower level is only the will looking for a reason and proving it right, like a bribe. When the will is put into practice, the order turns over into *yosher*, with the deed outside. Of the *Ein Sof* itself nothing may be said; speech begins with *Adam Kadmon*.

terms.gloss: the primordial will: the simple will come up in a thought, a copy whose content is the Essence's own, still a will for Himself
circles (singular igul); sefiros where each cause surrounds its effect and the highest is the finest: the will and its daydream
straightness; the sefiros as the upper dressed in the lower, where the will is innermost and the deed outside: the will being done
the Ancient of the Ancients: the ratzon kadum as the delight of all delights, the Atik of every Atik down to each detail
the hidden Ancient One: Keser of Adam Kadmon, already an Atik but still hidden
the holy Ancient One: Atik and Arich of Atzilus, the whole Keser, where the will and delight are revealed
the will of all wills: the ratzon kadum, revealed in the forehead of Atika Kadisha
the forehead: the one part of the skull that is seen, where the will shows
the King's delight in Himself, before the tzimtzum, higher than Atika d'Atikin
a bribe: the will bribing the mind to find it a reason; rationalization
a reason; there is no reason for a will, and the reason never reaches it
He engraved an engraving; the letters before the tzimtzum, still part of the mind, not a separate thought

sections.title: The Kav in circles and in straightness: the question the chapter opens
sections.summary: The chapter turns to the details of the *Kav*: it comes as an inner light, becomes a circle, and so on. The *Etz Chaim* says that in the circles the highest is the finest, and in *yosher* (straightness) the opposite.

phrases.he: (יז) והנה מעתה יש להבין בפרטי ענין הקו
phrases.en: (17) Now, from here on, we have to understand the details of the matter of the *Kav* (the line),

phrases.he: כמו שהוא בבחינת עגולים כו'.
phrases.en: as it is in the aspect of *igulim* (circles).

phrases.he: והנה תחלה יש להקדים בבחינת ראשית הקו הזה
phrases.en: But first we must preface [a word] on the beginning of this *Kav*,

phrases.he: שבא בבחינת אור פנימי
phrases.en: which comes as *or pnimi* (inner light),

phrases.he: ואחר כך מתעגל
phrases.en: and afterwards becomes a circle,

phrases.he: ונמשך בבחינת אור פנימי
phrases.en: and draws on again as inner light,

phrases.he: וחוזר ומתעגל כו'
phrases.en: and again becomes a circle.

phrases.he: ומבואר בעץ חיים שבבחינת עשר ספירות דעגולים,
phrases.en: It is explained in *Etz Chaim* that in the ten sefiros of the circles,

phrases.he: העליון מכולם משובח מכולם והפנימי מכולם גרוע כו',
phrases.en: the highest of them all is the finest of them all, and the innermost of them all is the poorest;

phrases.he: ובבחינת עשר ספירות דיושר להיפך,
phrases.en: and in the ten sefiros of *yosher* (straightness) it is the opposite:

phrases.he: העליון גרוע והפנימי משובח כו'.
phrases.en: the highest is the poorest, and the innermost the finest.

blocks.text: The class opens by reading the first lines straight through: from here on we have to understand the details of the *Kav* as it is in *igulim*. First, the beginning of the *Kav* comes as an inner light, then becomes a circle, then draws on as an inner light and again becomes a circle. And the *Etz Chaim* says that in the circles **the highest of them all is the finest of them all**, and in *yosher* it is the other way round. The explanation follows.

sections.title: The ratzon kadum: the simple will come up in a thought, still for Himself
sections.summary: The *ratzon kadum* is the same simple will that was already decided in the Essence, once it comes up in a thought. Its letters are a copy, no longer the letters of the Essence, yet its content is exactly the same; and it is still a will for His own enjoyment, not for the thing.

phrases.he: וביאור הדברים, הנה ידוע שבחינת רצון קדום זה,
phrases.en: The explanation of the matter: it is known that this *ratzon kadum* (primordial will),

phrases.he: הגם שלגבי בחינת רצון הפשוט המוחלט בעצמות
phrases.en: even though, compared to the simple and absolute will in the Essence,

phrases.he: נקרא התפשטות רצון,
phrases.en: it is called a *hispashtus* (spreading out) of will,

phrases.he: אבל עדיין הוא בהעלם ולא בגלוי כלל
phrases.en: it is still hidden and not revealed at all;

phrases.he: כי אינו רק השפעת והמשכת רצון הפשוט של חפץ חסד שהוחלט בעצמות מכבר,
phrases.en: for it is only the flow and drawing down of the simple will of *chafetz chesed* (desire for kindness) that was already decided in the Essence,

phrases.he: כך יהיה בפועל ממש
phrases.en: that so it shall be, in actual fact.

phrases.he: ומיד שעולה במחשבה זאת שיהיה הכל,
phrases.en: And as soon as this comes up in thought, that everything shall be,

phrases.he: הוא הנקרא מחשבה ורצון קדום
phrases.en: that is what is called the primordial thought and will,

phrases.he: שכולל כל מה שבתוכו רצונות פרטים
phrases.en: which includes everything within it, particular wills,

phrases.he: כנזכר לעיל במשל הבנין
phrases.en: as explained above in the analogy of the building.

blocks.text: It is just simply the same *ratzon hapashut* (simple will) that was already decided, that this is the way it should be. When it comes up in an actual *machshava* (thought), that is what is called the *ratzon kadum*, the primordial will, which includes within it all the particular wills.

A *machshava* means that the thought is a separate thing, in letters. It is the same as writing: the writing is a separate thing from the original *sechel* (intellect) itself. The only difference is that a *machshava* comes up, as it were, inside of himself.

blocks.question: Was the glif glifu (the engraving of letters before the tzimtzum) not also like that?
blocks.text: No. The *glif glifu* is not really a separate *machshava*. It is still part of the *sechel* itself, the way a thing is still part of the mind, rather than an actual thought.

blocks.question: And what about the reshimu?
blocks.text: The *tzimtzum* happened, and the thought was there in the *glif glifu*. The *reshimu* (impression) is also the *glif glifu*, only the light of the *Atzmus* went out of it. But it is still how it was inside of Himself. So it is really considered that the *reshimu* is still the *Atzmus*.

From the *reshimu* it went out in a line of *hispashtus* to the *ratzon kadum*, the *machshava kduma*. These are again the same letters as the *reshimu*; and the letters of the *reshimu* were *mamash* the letters of the *glif glifu*, only the light went out of them. The letters of the *machshava kduma* are different letters. That is why it is called *Atik*: it is a copy (*ha'atka*) of those letters, not *mamash* those letters, no longer exactly the letters of the *Atzmus*. Still, it is the *machshava* of the *Atzmus*, only already the thought of the *Atzmus* as it is going to go to the outside. It is already coming out, "if that makes any sense".

Compared to the *Atzmus* it is already *mamash* a different thing, and yet it is really still the *machshava* of the *Atzmus*. The *Atzmus* is gone and the light of the *Atzmus* is gone, as in the *reshimu*, and even the letters are not the same original letters anymore; but as far as its content goes it is exactly the same thing. Nothing really changed, even though it is just a copy.

So **that is what is called the primordial thought and will**, and it is *mamash* the same thing, including all the particular wills. Compared to the *Atzmus* it is called a spreading out of will. But it is really still just for Himself, not for the thing yet: for His own enjoyment. As with a chair: it is not really the chair He wants, it is His own sitting. That is the analogy of the building.

phrases.he: אם כן עדיין רצון קדום זה הכל בעצמו
phrases.en: If so, this *ratzon kadum* is still all within Himself,

phrases.he: בלתי התגלות לחוץ,
phrases.en: without being revealed to the outside.

blocks.text: So the *ratzon kadum* is really still all inside of Himself, **without being revealed to the outside**.

sections.title: Everything is made from it: knowing Himself, He knows every detail, down to the end
sections.summary: From the *ratzon kadum*, which is really Himself, everything is made afterwards, as from knowing a man you know his house. Every detail, down to a bug or a drunk in the street, is a detail of the King and deserves respect; and the end of the deed, the finished house, came up first of all.

phrases.he: אבל ממנו נעשה הכל אחר כך
phrases.en: But from it everything is made afterwards.

blocks.text: **But from it everything is made afterwards**. This is the matter of "by knowing Himself, He knows everything". What does that mean, and how could He know everything? It was said that all the details were really there. But, you say, they were not there in the way they are made out.

blocks.title: The size of his pants
blocks.text: The details really are there. If you know the guy, you know what size pants he needs. How do you know these are the pants he would need? "Well, I know him." You measure him, and you know what size pants he needs. In the same way, over here He is still not considered to know anything outside of Himself.

blocks.title: A house for a bird
blocks.text: It is like the analogy of the building. Over here there is still no will for a swimming pool; there is a will for swimming. There is no will for a kitchen; there is a will for eating. There is no will for a bedroom; there is a will for sleeping. So how does he know? If you know him, you will know what kind of bedroom he wants. If he is a bird, his bedroom is going to have a stick in it. It won't look like our bedroom. And his house will be without stairs: you come in from the top floor. It will be just different, because he is different. If you know him, you know what the house is going to be like. The thing he knows is not the house yet; it is him.

**But from it everything is made afterwards**: from the way he is, that is how everything is made afterwards. That is not quite what it says, though. It says from this *ratzon kadum*; but in this *ratzon kadum* it is really Himself.

phrases.he: וזהו כי הוא אמר,
phrases.en: And this is "For He said,"

phrases.he: במחשבה הקדומה,
phrases.en: in the primordial thought,

phrases.he: ויהי כו'
phrases.en: "and it was."

blocks.text: He said it in the *machshava kduma*, **"and it was."** What did He say in the *machshava kduma*? That was the whole thing. As far as the *Aibershter* (G-d) is concerned, He said it in the *machshava kduma* and finished. Then it came out by itself already.

phrases.he: ונקרא חיי כל העולמים
phrases.en: And it is called the life of all the worlds,

phrases.he: מראש דאדם קדמון עד עקב אדם קדמון בסוף עשיה,
phrases.en: from the head of *Adam Kadmon* to the heel of *Adam Kadmon* at the end of *Asiya*;

phrases.he: והיינו כל היצור לא נכחד כו'
phrases.en: and this is "No creature is hidden [from You]": nothing is missing;

phrases.he: שאין פרט היותר אחרון שלא קדם להיות ברצון ובמחשבה זו
phrases.en: for there is no detail, even the very last, that was not first in this will and thought.

blocks.text: **"No creature is hidden [from You]"** means that nothing is missing. In preparing the final thing, every detail of the final thing has to come with a detail of the *Atzmus* that it is being prepared for.

blocks.title: The king does not buy off the rack
blocks.text: Remember, we are talking about a king, and for a king everything is going to be custom, exactly how he wants it. He is not buying a suit off the rack. When we go and buy a suit, it is not made exactly; the tailor goes and stretches it here and does it there, and even then you don't get *mamash* exactly the color you want. Same thing with the house. Here we are talking about the original thing, exactly what he wants. In us, too, as will be said later, there is exactly what you want, "except that you can't necessarily afford it." But a king gets exactly what he wants. When he wants some wine, he gets exactly what he wants, even if it costs a thousand dollars a bottle, and his clothes will be exactly what he wants. So every little detail goes according to a detail in the *machshava kduma*, which goes according to Himself. There is not one little thing left out.

So the creature, the *yetzur*, is a very important thing here. Even if you see a bug, that bug is somehow an enclothement of some detail upstairs. Anything. It says, "No creature is hidden from You": nothing is missing. There cannot be any creature that does not fit some detail upstairs.

blocks.question: What about the yucky things?
blocks.text: Even the yucky things are still yucky according to something upstairs.

blocks.title: The Atari game in the king's house
blocks.text: Even to the point where you say: look at Amalek. How can you say it fits Him, when the whole thing is to kill him? So look at the guy's house. In the guy's house he has a computer arcade, an Atari game, and that Atari game is fighting against him. The thing that fights against him fits something in his character. It *davka* has to fight against him; you don't want an Atari game that just says, "Hi, how you doing?" You want it *davka* to fight against you. That fits the *midda* of *netzach* (victory).

So you cannot have any little thing in the world that is not really it. It is not just an enclothement of it; it really is it. It is *mamash* the *machshava kduma*, which is *mamash* the *Aibershter*: it is like the stamp of the *Aibershter*, and the stamp of the *Aibershter* means it is *mamash* the *Aibershter*'s name.

So in terms of respect, you have to respect everything. If you see a squirrel, you are seeing G-d. "What do you mean?" You have to think about it. Anything that is in what He wanted is part of Him; it fits some part of Him. As with clothing: there is no part of the clothing that does not fit some part of the king. If you spit on a part of the clothing, even on the shoe, you are spitting on the king. So you have to have a lot of respect. That is what **"No creature is hidden [from You]"** tells you: when you are looking at anything, you are literally looking at the *Aibershter*.

**for there is no detail, even the very last, that was not first in this will and thought.** There is nothing that was not originally over there. So it doesn't matter. You can see "some stupid dirty bum walking down the street half drunk", and you say, "What about him?" Yes: even the very last detail could not be there unless it was first over there.

sensitivity.reason: Calls a drunk man in the street "some stupid dirty bum".
sensitivity.publishable: **for there is no detail, even the very last, that was not first in this will and thought.** There is nothing that was not originally over there. So it doesn't matter. You can see a man walking down the street half drunk, and you say, "What about him?" Yes: even the very last detail could not be there unless it was first over there.

phrases.he: ואדרבה סוף מעשה,
phrases.en: Just the opposite: the end of the deed,

phrases.he: כמו בסוף אלף הז',
phrases.en: as at the end of the seventh millennium,

phrases.he: עלה במחשבה קדומה זו תחלה
phrases.en: came up first in this primordial thought,

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב במקום אחר באריכות
phrases.en: as is written elsewhere at length.

blocks.text: Not only that. It is not that *davka* the worlds of *Atzilus* were really over there and we are not so really over there. **Just the opposite: the end of the deed … came up first in this primordial thought.** You see this in clothing as well.

blocks.title: The outermost clothes
blocks.text: It is *davka* the most external clothes that represent the king more. You yourself can't go out into the street in your inner clothes, your underwear, because your inner clothes are not *mamash* the real honor. The real honor is the most external clothes, the ones you wear over them, on the total outside.

blocks.title: The wallpaper, not the studs
blocks.text: The same with a house. In terms of holding the house up, the actual structure is the cement and the studs: you have seen a house being built, the skeleton, with wires running all over the place and plumbing pipes. But the real thing that you wanted is *davka* the finished product. The thing you really wanted is the wallpaper. When he thought of a house, he thought of a room surrounded with wallpaper; that behind the wallpaper there has to be drywall, and behind the drywall studs and whatever else, is beside the point. When he went with his wife to plan it, they didn't talk about the studs. They talked about wallpaper, and a carpet on the floor or parquet, and the ceiling was mainly the paint, not so much the drywall.

blocks.title: The chandelier and the decorators
blocks.text: As we said, the real thing is that he wanted to please his wife, and the main thing she was thinking about was the fixtures on the ceiling, the beautiful chandelier: the most external, final level, done at the very end of the making. First you put up the studs, then the drywall, and as far as the construction crew is concerned it is already a finished building. Then you walk in with the wife, and she says: "Look at this place. There is dust all over the floor, and it's not even a floor yet, it's just a piece of plywood!" Now come the final touches, when you bring in the decorators. And in the first thought, that is the way you saw it, not the stuff behind it.

sensitivity.reason: Built on a stock picture of the wife who cares about the chandelier and is unimpressed by the bare building.
sensitivity.publishable: The real thing is that he wanted to please his wife, and what they were both thinking about was the fixtures on the ceiling, the beautiful chandelier: the most external, final level, done at the very end of the making. First you put up the studs, then the drywall, and as far as the construction crew is concerned it is already a finished building. But walk in and look: there is dust all over the floor, and it's not even a floor yet, just a piece of plywood. Now come the final touches, when you bring in the decorators. And in the first thought, that is the way you saw it, not the stuff behind it.

blocks.text: So here too the real thing is *davka* when the whole thing is finished: **as at the end of the seventh millennium**. Not only the end of the deed in the sense of the actual world being there, but even in terms of the physical world, the whole thing was how it is going to be at the end of the seventh millennium, "when we have already sat down and studied *Shaar HaYichud* for a thousand years. And not only *Shaar HaYichud*, but with all its commentaries, like *Ayin Beis* and stuff like that." When we will have had the thousand years of *Moshiach*, then it is already the thing that He wanted, "and then we can start on the fifty thousand jubilees." And this **came up first in this primordial thought, as is written elsewhere at length.**

sections.title: The Zohar's names: Atika d'Atikin, Atika Stima'a and Atika Kadisha
sections.summary: The *ratzon kadum* is *Atika d'Atikin*, the delight of all delights and the will of all wills, and *Atika Stima'a*, *Keser* of *Adam Kadmon*: still hidden, still for Himself. It is revealed in the *metzach* (forehead) of *Atika Kadisha*, *Atik* and *Arich* of *Atzilus*, where the will and delight for each world, and for each detail, come out.

phrases.he: (ובלשון הזהר נקרא עתיקא דעתיקין
phrases.en: (In the language of the *Zohar* it is called *Atika d'Atikin* (the Ancient of the Ancients)

phrases.he: או עתיקא סתימאה
phrases.en: or *Atika Stima'a* (the hidden Ancient One),

phrases.he: והוא בחינת רעוא דכל רעווין עילאין
phrases.en: and it is *Raava d'chol Raavin Ila'in*, the will of all the upper wills,

phrases.he: דאתגליין במצחא דעתיקא קדישא כו'
phrases.en: which are revealed in the *metzach* (forehead) of *Atika Kadisha* (the holy Ancient One);

phrases.he: כי ברצון מלובש התענוג,
phrases.en: for the delight is dressed in the will,

phrases.he: והיו לאחדים ממש
phrases.en: and they become *mamash* one.

blocks.text: In the language of the *Zohar*, this *machshava kduma* is called *Atika d'Atikin* or *Atika Stima'a*. It is the *taanug* (delight) of all the delights, or the hidden delight: not yet a delight for the outside, not a revealed delight. It is not a delight in the chair; it is a delight for Himself, to sit.

Besides being called the delight of all delights, it is also called **the will of all the upper wills**, revealed in the *metzach* of *Atika Kadisha*. Why both names? **for the delight is dressed in the will, and they become *mamash* one.** It is *mamash* one thing.

phrases.he: וברצון הפשוט ההיולי
phrases.en: And in the simple, *hiyuli* (raw, all-including) will

phrases.he: שבחפץ חסד ההיולי (הנזכר לעיל באות יוד ואות יא)
phrases.en: of the *hiyuli* *chafetz chesed* (mentioned above in sections 10 and 11)

phrases.he: היה כלול בו התענוג הפשוט שבעצמות
phrases.en: was included the simple delight in the Essence,

phrases.he: שנקרא שעשועי המלך בעצמותו כו'
phrases.en: which is called *sha'ashuei hamelech* (the King's delight) in Himself;

phrases.he: וגם בג' מדריגות עד שבא בדבר פרט,
phrases.en: and also in the three levels, until it comes to a particular thing,

phrases.he: אנא אמלוך,
phrases.en: *Ana Emloch* (I shall rule),

phrases.he: שזה בחינת מלכות דאין סוף שלפני הצמצום
phrases.en: which is *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof* before the *tzimtzum*,

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב שם
phrases.en: as is written there,

phrases.he: הכל בחינת שעשועי המלך בעצמו בטהירו עילאה
phrases.en: it is all the King's delight in Himself, in the *tehiru ila'a* (the upper purity).

blocks.text: This, the King's delight in Himself, is *mamash* even more than *Atika d'Atikin*. *Atika d'Atikin* is already the actual delight, compared to the delight as it was there; over there it was *mamash* prior, still the *Atzmus*. And there it is not just that it is not composite: over there it is *hayah k'lo hayah* (as if it were not there). And so in all **three levels**, *Yachid*, *Echad* and *Kadmon*, until *Ana Emloch*, *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof* before the *tzimtzum*: **it is all the King's delight in Himself**.

phrases.he: אך עתיקא דעתיקין מקור כל התענוגים
phrases.en: But *Atika d'Atikin*, the source of all delights,

phrases.he: או רעוא דכל רעויין כו',
phrases.en: or *Raava d'chol Raavin*,

phrases.he: היינו בבחינת הקו שאחר הצמצום
phrases.en: is in the *Kav* after the *tzimtzum*,

phrases.he: שכולל כמה רצונות ותענוגים שעתידים לבוא בגלוי
phrases.en: which includes many wills and delights that are to come into revelation.

blocks.text: That is the actual will for Himself. But it is a will for Himself in relation to the *Atzmus*: for Himself, for a house. It is a preceding will for a house. "What do you mean, a will for a house? I thought you said it's not really a will for a house." Yes: it is not really a will for a house; it is a will for a home. A home means it is really a will for himself, but already in relationship to a house.

So it is not like the *ratzon hapashut*. The *ratzon hapashut* is not a will for Himself; it is Himself. The simple delight is *mamash* Himself: not a will or a delight for Himself, *mamash* Himself. And this one is the will for Himself, **which includes many wills and delights that are to come into revelation.**

phrases.he: ועתיקא סתימאה הוא בבחינת כתר דאדם קדמון
phrases.en: And *Atika Stima'a* is *Keser* of *Adam Kadmon*,

phrases.he: שהוא בהעלם הרצון והתענוג לעצמו עדיין,
phrases.en: where the will and delight are still hidden, for Himself,

phrases.he: רק שחושב להיות הדבר כך בפועל הגילוי
phrases.en: only He thinks that the thing should be so in actual revelation,

phrases.he: כמו להיות גילוי הרצון והתענוג להאציל עשר ספירות כו'
phrases.en: such as that there be a revelation of the will and delight to emanate ten sefiros

phrases.he: (ולכך נקרא עתיקא סתימאה בחינת העלם לגלוי על כל פנים
phrases.en: (and that is why it is called *Atika Stima'a*: a hiddenness [ready] for revelation, at any rate;

phrases.he: מה שאין כן ראשית הקו נקרא סתימא דכל סתימין
phrases.en: whereas the beginning of the *Kav* is called *stima d'chol stimin* (the most hidden of all hidden),

phrases.he: דגם מחשבה דאדם קדמון לא תפיס ביה כו')
phrases.en: which even the thought of *Adam Kadmon* does not grasp);

phrases.he: ולהיות הרצון והתענוג לברוא כו'
phrases.en: and that there be the will and delight to create.

blocks.text: It is really still for Himself, **only He thinks that the thing should be so in actual revelation**. It is not just *mamash* Himself; it is *mamash* Himself thinking in terms of sitting, so that there will have to be a chair, even though He is not really thinking of a chair.

**that there be a revelation of the will and delight to emanate ten sefiros**: but it is not really the will for *Atzilus* yet. The *ratzon kadum* is called *Atika Stima'a*: it is already an *Atik*, but it is hidden. The very beginning of the *Kav* is called *stima d'chol stimin*, which even *Atika Stima'a* cannot grasp. And the sentence reads on past the parenthesis: to emanate ten sefiros, **and that there be the will and delight to create.**

phrases.he: ועתיקא קדישא הוא התענוג שבחכמה
phrases.en: And *Atika Kadisha* is the delight in *chachma*,

phrases.he: והוא בחינת עתיק יומין ואריך אנפין דאצילות,
phrases.en: and it is *Atik Yomin* and *Arich Anpin* of *Atzilus*,

phrases.he: שהרצון והתענוג בא בגלוי
phrases.en: where the will and delight come into revelation,

phrases.he: כמו שיתבאר הכל דרך פרט)
phrases.en: as will all be explained in detail.)

blocks.question: What was said before, the will of all the upper wills revealed in the forehead of Atika Kadisha, seems to be a higher level than Atik and Arich of Atzilus?
blocks.text: *Atika Kadisha* is *Atik* and *Arich* of *Atzilus*, what is usually called *Atik* and *Arich*. No, it is not a higher level. *Atik* and *Arich* are the revealed delight and will; that is where the revelation is. *Raava d'chol Raavin* is the *machshava kduma*, which is hidden, and it is revealed in the *metzach* of *Atik*.

Even *Adam Kadmon* is called the hidden will. There is no actual revelation in *Adam Kadmon* of what it actually is; it is only in *Atik*. Some places say that *Atika Kadisha* is *Arich*; here it is explained better: *Atika Kadisha* means the whole *Keser*.

The next side opens with *Atika Kadisha* and the basic detail of it, the *metzach*. The *metzach* is the part of the *gulgoles* (skull) in front of the frontal lobe. The will is revealed in the *metzach*: when he has a certain kind of will, the will comes into the brain, but the brain is hidden, and the *metzach* is in front of the brain. We don't really notice it, but it is described in various places how the forehead lights up or gets sad.
blocks.outOfPlace: The next class (the second side of the tape) goes on with *Atika Kadisha* and its *metzach* before it rereads lines 21-23; kept here, in class order, under the passage being discussed.

blocks.title: Seeing through the hat
blocks.text: There is the thing that the big kabbalists can read your forehead. A man went to the *Rebbe*, having been told that the *Rebbe* can see on your forehead what you are thinking, and he went there with his hat pulled down. The *Rebbe* told him: "You think if I can see through your forehead, I can't see through your hat?" So the revelation of the will is in the forehead.
blocks.outOfPlace: The next class (the second side of the tape) goes on with *Atika Kadisha* and its *metzach* before it rereads lines 21-23; kept here, in class order, under the passage being discussed.

blocks.text: *Atik* in *Arich* is the will and delight revealed. So there is the will and delight to emanate *Atzilus*, then the will and delight to create, then for *Yetzira* and *Asiya*, all the way to the end. As said last time, the will for *Atzilus* is the will to figure out in his own head what it is that he really wants: that is a revealed will. This is called *Atika Stima'a*, and *Atika Kadisha* is the revealed *Atik*. *Atzilus* is where he planned the house in his own head; *Beriya* is where he goes to the architect, *Yetzira* where he goes to the draftsman, and *Asiya* where it goes to the contractor.
blocks.outOfPlace: The next class (the second side of the tape) goes on with *Atika Kadisha* and its *metzach* before it rereads lines 21-23; kept here, in class order, under the passage being discussed.

blocks.text: So there is no detail that is not really in there. And the intermediary levels, even though in a way they are not the actual intrinsic thing, only conduits to get to it, nonetheless have their own will and delight. In building a house, the planning too: he sits with his wife and they plan out what they want, and they get a big pleasure out of it. To the point that a person can get such a big pleasure out of planning that he never gets around to doing anything. "This is called daydreaming."
blocks.outOfPlace: The next class (the second side of the tape) goes on with *Atika Kadisha* and its *metzach* before it rereads lines 21-23; kept here, in class order, under the passage being discussed.

blocks.title: The rabbi and his gvir watch the yeshiva go up
blocks.text: "Like you're here, you start a *yeshiva* here", in a pretty new building. While it was being built, the rabbi would sometimes come with his big *gvir* (wealthy backer), and they would stand there and look at it, and you could see they were getting a big pleasure. It is just a building, the guys are building, what do they care? And the pleasure was not only that finally they would have the end product; it was from the building stage itself. So it has its own delight and will.
blocks.outOfPlace: The next class (the second side of the tape) goes on with *Atika Kadisha* and its *metzach* before it rereads lines 21-23; kept here, in class order, under the passage being discussed.

blocks.title: The artist's picture at the banquet
blocks.text: And even before that, when they first had the plan and the first banquet, there was the artist's representation the architect made of how the building is going to look. There was no building, nothing, not even the blueprint; just this picture, the concept of what the building would be like. And there was a big delight even in that.
blocks.outOfPlace: The next class (the second side of the tape) goes on with *Atika Kadisha* and its *metzach* before it rereads lines 21-23; kept here, in class order, under the passage being discussed.

blocks.text: There is a big delight even when he goes shopping for the car. "And especially you see this in women": there is a big delight for them in the actual shopping, and even before that, they can just sit around and talk about what they are planning to shop, especially for a house, when she is planning her house, how it is going to be. There is a big delight just in that.
blocks.outOfPlace: The next class (the second side of the tape) goes on with *Atika Kadisha* and its *metzach* before it rereads lines 21-23; kept here, in class order, under the passage being discussed.

sensitivity.reason: A generalisation that women take special delight in shopping and in planning the house.
sensitivity.publishable: There is a big delight even when one goes shopping for a car: a big delight in the actual shopping, and even before that, in sitting around and talking about what one is planning to buy, especially for a house, planning how it is going to be. There is a big delight just in that.

blocks.text: So there is a delight in *Atzilus*, a delight in *Beriya*, a delight in *Yetzira* and a delight in *Asiya*. But of all of them, the biggest delight is *davka* in the end of the deed, more than anything else: at the end of the seventh millennium, when it is all accomplished.
blocks.outOfPlace: The next class (the second side of the tape) goes on with *Atika Kadisha* and its *metzach* before it rereads lines 21-23; kept here, in class order, under the passage being discussed.

blocks.question: How come he always says that we, now, are the biggest delight, even more than the end of the seventh millennium?
blocks.text: Where do you get a bigger delight? *Chanuka* is coming up now. Do you get the biggest delight when the kid graduates from *yeshiva*, or from college "by the *goyim*", or when he is in the *Chanuka* play and you dress him up like a latke? Really the biggest delight is when you dress him up like a latke. Look at the parents at the graduating exercises of the final year of *yeshiva*, and look at the parents at the *Chanuka* play, where he is dressed up like a latke: there is a bigger delight when he is dressed up like a latke. "And that's who we are: we're dressed up like a latke."
blocks.outOfPlace: The next class (the second side of the tape) goes on with *Atika Kadisha* and its *metzach* before it rereads lines 21-23; kept here, in class order, under the passage being discussed.

blocks.text: The *metzach* is the will. He reads it from the *Zohar* (*parshas Naso*): the forehead, which is called will, is the revelation of the whole head and skull. Not that the skull is the will: the *metzach* is the part of the skull that you see, the revelation of the skull, and so the revelation of the will. The rest is covered up by hair. The only part of the skull you actually see is the forehead, and not only that, it is the part in front, facing you. You can see a person scratch his forehead; when he thinks, he looks up. There are all kinds of things that, if you know, you can see on the forehead.
blocks.outOfPlace: The next class (the second side of the tape) goes on with *Atika Kadisha* and its *metzach* before it rereads lines 21-23; kept here, in class order, under the passage being discussed.

blocks.question: Where does this parenthesis start, and where does it end?
blocks.text: Reading lines 21-23 again: should a parenthesis open before *Atika Kadisha*, with **as will all be explained in detail** as its end? The parenthesis from *ve'lachach* to "even the thought of *Adam Kadmon* does not grasp it" ends by itself. "No, but this parenthesis starts *uvilshon haZohar*, it starts all the way up": the one that ends at **in detail** begins at "In the language of the *Zohar*" in line 14. "Yeah, it's so weird." "This whole thing has been a parenthesis."
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 026 rereads lines 21-23 in one breath (w1248-1279, aligned to line 21); the question is about the parenthesis that closes at the end of line 23.

blocks.text: That is the whole matter here. The *ratzon kadum* is still a will for Himself, and it includes everything. It is called *Atika d'Atikin*, the *Atik* of all the *Atiks*: the will and delight to emanate, the *Atik* of *Atzilus*; the will and delight to create, the *Atik* of *Beriya*; and the *Atik* of *Yetzira* and of *Asiya*. And also of all the sub-*Atiks*: within *Atzilus* each one, *chachma* and *bina* of each level, has a *Keser*, and so on to all the details; each detail of a detail has a *Keser*. It is the *Atik* and *Arich* of all the *Atiks* and *Ariks*: the delight and will for every delight and will, to the last detail, is this delight and will.
blocks.outOfPlace: Said right after class 026 rereads lines 21-23 and settles the parenthesis: the summing-up of what these lines say about *Atika d'Atikin*.

blocks.question: If everything is there for a delight, where do the yucky things come from, and why do they exist?
blocks.text: There is no detail whose delight and will was not included in it; even what is yucky is over there. A will has a positive and a negative. A *chazir* (pig), a "fooey" thing: that is where it came from. Up there there is a negative delight and will for it. "Wouldn't a negative delight and will be pain, an absence of will, the opposite of will?" That is what it is: a predisposition to hate this thing. Whatever comes out and has an existence is there because there is a delight for it; it is not because it exists that you hate it and destroy it, but because in the *machshava kduma* it was a hateful thing. "Okay, but why does it exist?" It is an Atari game. It exists in order to blast it.
blocks.outOfPlace: Asked right after class 026 rereads lines 21-23, about their point that every detail's delight and will is included in *Atika d'Atikin*.

blocks.text: Like Amalek, the ultimate bad. Why does Amalek exist? In order to have the *mitzva* to kill Amalek. That's it. Since it is the opposite of the delight, there is an actual delight in getting rid of it, a positive delight in Amalek's destruction: two negatives make a positive. When you get rid of a bad thing, you get a delight. "Why make it in the first place?" "Sounds like fun to me." If you don't like something, why make it? Because there is more of a delight in destroying it. "But you made the house; it's not like He hates it so much that He gets a delight in destroying it." "Yeah, right, I mean, that's the thing." We say: we don't have a choice; when there is a bad thing, we hope we can get rid of it. But if you are the one who made the world, why make these bad things in the first place, and not make it already perfect? So look at the guy's house. He has this Atari game with weird creatures that he has to battle against and destroy, and there is a delight in destroying them. That is what they were made for: for destruction.
blocks.outOfPlace: Continues the question on lines 21-23 asked right after class 026 rereads them.

sections.title: Circles one beneath the other: a will that bribes the mind to find it a reason
sections.summary: In the circles each cause surrounds its effect, and the effect never reaches it. A revealed will shows how: it comes first as one undivided will, and its *chachma* and *bina* are only a will to find it a reason and to prove the reason right, as in a bribe, or in politics. All of it is the will for Himself, down to the end of the deed, which is the innermost.

phrases.he: והנה בחינת עשר ספירות דעגולים זה תחת זה הוא כידוע,
phrases.en: Now, the ten sefiros of the circles, one beneath the other, are as is known:

phrases.he: שכל עילה מקפת לעלול
phrases.en: every cause surrounds its effect,

phrases.he: ועלול לא ישיג לעילה שלו כי אם בריחוק מקום ממנו,
phrases.en: and the effect does not reach its cause except at a distance of place from it,

phrases.he: כאשר יהיה האופן בתוך כו'
phrases.en: "as a wheel would be within [a wheel]."

blocks.text: The tape picks up with the reading. Until now he was talking about the *machshava kduma*; now he is going to explain the circles and *yosher*. **every cause surrounds its effect, and the effect does not reach its cause except at a distance of place from it.**

phrases.he: ויובן זה מהרצון הבא בגלוי גמור
phrases.en: This can be understood from the will that comes in complete revelation:

phrases.he: שגם שכלול הרצון הזה מי', חכמה ומדות,
phrases.en: although this will includes ten, *chachma* and *middos*,

phrases.he: אבל תחלתו בא רק בהסכם א'
phrases.en: at its start it comes only as one consent,

phrases.he: בלי התחלקות ניכר בו
phrases.en: with no division noticeable in it.

phrases.he: והוא הנקרא עיגול רצון כללי
phrases.en: And this is called the circle of general will,

phrases.he: מקיף לכל מה שבא בתוכו מכחו דוקא,
phrases.en: surrounding all that comes within it, *davka* from its power,

phrases.he: אך בריחוק מקום
phrases.en: but at a distance of place.

blocks.text: Here we are talking about the *ratzon kadum*, and now he makes an analogy from the revealed will. When you first have a will, it is just a will. Even though it has ten sefiros, at the beginning it comes as one consent, one will. So even a lower will, a revealed will, comes first as a general circle, **surrounding all that comes within it**.

phrases.he: כמו הטעם ושכל לרצון זה, שנקרא עלול שלו
phrases.en: Like the *taam* (reason) and intellect for this will, which is called its effect:

phrases.he: אי אפשר שיהיה קרוב בערך אל עילתו, שהוא הרצון,
phrases.en: it cannot be close in value to its cause, which is the will,

phrases.he: כי הרי אין טעם לרצון כלל כידוע,
phrases.en: for there is no reason for a will at all, as is known,

phrases.he: ולעולם לא ישיגנו
phrases.en: and it will never reach it;

phrases.he: אבל מכל מקום מכח הרצון נעשה עיגול החכמה גם כן
phrases.en: but nevertheless, from the power of the will the circle of *chachma* is made too,

phrases.he: בלי התחלקות ניכר ליה כו'
phrases.en: also with no division noticeable in it.

blocks.text: Really, **there is no reason for a will**. The reason cannot get close to the will, because there is really no actual reason for a will. It is not possible to understand it, because it has no *sechel*: there is no *sechel* to a will.

**the circle of *chachma***: it is not actually *chachma*. It is a circle of *chachma*, meaning a will of *chachma*: either the *chachma* to come up with a way to get what is willed, or else a *chachma* to rationalize the will.

phrases.he: כמו משל השוחד,
phrases.en: As in the analogy of the *shochad* (the bribe):

phrases.he: שימצא טעם לרצון
phrases.en: that it should find a reason for the will.

blocks.title: The bribe
blocks.text: **As in the analogy of the *shochad***: the bribe is that he should find a reason for the will. That is what is called rationalization.

blocks.question: Is this like the three ways Arich is dressed in Abba, where chesed and gevura of Arich are dressed in Abba, and chachma is like a puppet for the will?
blocks.text: This is higher. We are not even talking about *Abba* yet; we are talking about the will itself. In the will itself, it is a bribe: he wants to have a reason, he wants to come up with a reason. It is not actual *chachma* yet. Somebody asks him why he wants this thing, and he wants to be able to come up with a reason why he wants it, although really there is no reason.

phrases.he: וגם שבטעם זה כלול גם כן מיו''ד, רצון ושכל ומדות,
phrases.en: And although this reason too includes ten, will, intellect and *middos*,

phrases.he: אבל נעשה בבחינת כללי כו'
phrases.en: it is made in a general way;

phrases.he: ועל דרך זה לא ישיגנו העיגול דבינה שנעשה מכחו,
phrases.en: in the same way the circle of *bina*, which is made from its power, does not reach it;

phrases.he: ועל דרך זה המדות זה תחת זה עד סוף מעשה
phrases.en: and in the same way the *middos*, one beneath the other, down to the end of the deed,

phrases.he: שהוא עיגול האחרון
phrases.en: which is the last circle.

blocks.text: The reason has to include will, intellect and *middos*, but **it is made in a general way**: basically it is just a will to have a reason for the will. And **in the same way the circle of *bina***: a will to come up with an analysis for the reason.

You find this in politics. A person wants something, and he comes up with a reason why; they come up with a reason why their policy has to be correct. A guy wants to be president. Why does he want to be president? There is a whole thing: because of this and because of that, and he feels that he can help the country. "It's not really true. He really wants to be president."

sensitivity.reason: Says that a man who runs for president only wants to be president and his reasons are not true.
sensitivity.publishable: You find this in public life too. A person wants something, and he comes up with a reason why, and a reason why his position has to be correct. Why does he want it? There is a whole thing: because of this and because of that. But really he simply wants it, and the reasons come after.

blocks.text: And once they come up with a reason, for a certain policy for instance, they come up with a study. The study is set up to analyze the thing and to prove it. In *yosher* a study could prove that the thing was really wrong. In the circles, the whole job of the *bina* is only to prove that the *chachma* was right, and the whole job of the *chachma* is to prove that there really was a reason for the will, that the will does make sense.

**and in the same way the *middos*, one beneath the other, down to the end of the deed**. You see the same thing in politics. It could be a guy you can't stand, but he's a Republican and you're a Republican, so you like him, just because he's a Republican. So why do you like him?

sensitivity.reason: A partisan example: liking a man one cannot stand because he is a Republican.
sensitivity.publishable: **and in the same way the *middos*, one beneath the other, down to the end of the deed**. You see the same thing in any loyalty: it could be a man you can't stand, but he is on your side, so you like him, just because he is on your side. So why do you like him?

phrases.he: והכל ברצונו לעצמו
phrases.en: And all of it is in His will for Himself,

phrases.he: כלול הכל עד סוף מעשה
phrases.en: including everything down to the end of the deed,

phrases.he: שהוא הפנימי מכולם כו'
phrases.en: which is the innermost of them all.

blocks.text: None of this whole thing is actually any kind of *sechel* or *midda*. They are all the will itself, still only the will for Himself, **down to the end of the deed, which is the innermost of them all**: all the way to where He thinks inside of Himself how wonderful it would be to actually have a thing like this happen. That is the innermost of all of them.

sections.title: The ratzon kadum is the daydream; doing it turns the order over into yosher
sections.summary: The *ratzon kadum* has the same ten circles, a dream of the end of the deed. When the will comes to be done, the order is reversed: the will hides in the intellect, the intellect in the *middos*, and the deed, the lowest, stands on the outside and on top.

phrases.he: וכך הוא ברצון הנעלם הנקרא רצון הקדום הנזכר לעיל,
phrases.en: And so it is in the hidden will called the *ratzon kadum* mentioned above,

phrases.he: מקור כל הרצונות
phrases.en: the source of all wills:

phrases.he: כלול מי׳ ספירות על דרך זה,
phrases.en: it includes ten sefiros in this way,

phrases.he: עיגול בתוך עיגול עד עיגול דסוף מעשה,
phrases.en: circle within circle, down to the circle of the end of the deed,

phrases.he: שהוא הרצון לסוף מעשה,
phrases.en: which is the will for the end of the deed,

phrases.he: להיות כל אשר חפץ עושה בפועל ממש כו'
phrases.en: that all He desires He does, in actual fact;

phrases.he: והעיגול העליון הכולל הכל הוא רצון הקדום הנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: and the uppermost circle, which includes everything, is the *ratzon kadum* mentioned above.

blocks.text: The way a revealed will comes, the same is in the hidden will called the *ratzon kadum*: all ten sefiros, **circle within circle, down to the circle of the end of the deed**. It is not actually a circle of deed; it is a will for the end of the deed, **that all He desires He does**, and basically the whole thing is nothing but a daydream.

phrases.he: וכשבא הרצון לעצמו הזה להיות בפועל ממש
phrases.en: And when this will for Himself comes to be in actual fact,

phrases.he: הרי הוא להיפוך
phrases.en: it is the opposite:

blocks.text: **when this will for Himself comes to be in actual fact**: in order to have *yosher* you have to have circles first, because the circles are the daydream, the ambitions. Without the circles you would not have the *yosher*: without the first will and all the wills inside it, all the way down to the will for the deed. The *Malchus* of the circles becomes the *Keser* of *yosher*.

When it goes all the way to the end of the deed, he is sitting around daydreaming about the thing, how nice it would be. And then from that he says, "You know, but let's actually do it." Then **it is the opposite**.

phrases.he: שהרצון מתעלם ומתלבש בשכל
phrases.en: the will is hidden and dressed in the intellect,

phrases.he: והשכל מקיפו
phrases.en: and the intellect surrounds it.

blocks.title: The kid who wants a bicycle
blocks.text: A guy has a will for a house. Why does he have a will for a house? There is really no reason. But it makes up a will to have a *sechel*, so that he will be able to give you a reason. Like a kid who tells his father he wants a bicycle. Why does he want a bicycle? Because he wants a bicycle. "Oh, he wants a bicycle because then he'll be able to drive to school, and then he'll be able to do this." It's all not really true.

All the way down to the will for the deed itself, he is sitting around dreaming how nice it will be to have a house. And in the daydream the house is an infinite house, because that is how it is in the will. Then he decides: "You know, let's go and do the actual thing." So now he has to think. He has to get rid of the will and see what is really going on here. How much money does he have? Can he really have a house like this? The *sechel* has to take over: **the will is hidden and dressed in the intellect, and the intellect surrounds it.**

phrases.he: והשכל מתעלם ומתלבש במדות זה תחת זה עד סוף מעשה,
phrases.en: And the intellect is hidden and dressed in the *middos*, one beneath the other, down to the end of the deed,

phrases.he: הוא העליון מהכל
phrases.en: which is the uppermost of all;

phrases.he: דהיינו כח המעשה בפועל ממש
phrases.en: that is, the power of action, in actual fact:

phrases.he: הרי בו מלובש המחשבה
phrases.en: in it is dressed the thought,

phrases.he: ובמחשבה מלובש המדות
phrases.en: and in the thought the *middos*,

phrases.he: ובמדות מלובש החכמה ובינה
phrases.en: and in the *middos* *chachma* and *bina*,

phrases.he: ובחכמה מלובש הרצון והתענוג
phrases.en: and in *chachma* the will and the delight.

phrases.he: ונמצא פנימי מכולם הוא הרצון והתענוג,
phrases.en: So the innermost of all is the will and the delight,

phrases.he: וחיצון שבכולם הוא המעשה גרוע כו'
phrases.en: and the outermost of all is the deed, the lowest thing.

phrases.he: והוא בבחינת היושר כשבא בבחינת התלבשות העליון בתחתון כו'
phrases.en: And this is in *yosher*, when it comes as the upper dressing in the lower.

blocks.text: Then the *sechel*, the *chachma*, has to be actually hidden and dressed in a real analysis of what is really going on here, and then dressed in **the *middos*, one beneath the other, down to the end of the deed, which is the uppermost of all**.

**which is the uppermost of all**: it says that He made man *yashar* (straight), and when you look at a person you see him in the way of *yosher*. What you are seeing in a person is the deed, the outside of everything, which stands on top. Inside his deed are his emotions; from what he is doing and what he is saying you can tell…

**the power of action, in actual fact**, as you see in a person: in what a person does you can see what he is thinking, and in what he is thinking you can see what his *middos* are; in the *middos* are dressed *chachma* and *bina*, and in *chachma* the will and the delight. **So the innermost of all is the will and the delight, and the outermost of all is the deed, the lowest thing.** And it is actually an enclothement: the will is actually dressed in the *sechel*.

sections.title: Why the ratzon kadum comes in circles and through a short line, and where speaking begins
sections.summary: The *ratzon kadum*, still within Himself, comes in circles; to reach it from the *reshimu* takes a very great contraction, a short line. In the *Ein Sof* there is no up and down, and one may not speak even of its *Malchus*; speech begins with *Adam Kadmon*. The *ratzon kadum* is His great Name, and it is not a new thing: it is part of the true *ayin*.

phrases.he: אבל בבחינת רצון הקדום הנזכר לעיל שעדיין הוא בעצמו,
phrases.en: But in the *ratzon kadum* mentioned above, which is still within Himself,

phrases.he: על כן נמשך בבחינת עיגולים
phrases.en: it therefore comes in the way of circles,

phrases.he: שהעליון מהכל הוא העלם הרצון הכולל הזה
phrases.en: where the uppermost of all is the hiddenness of this all-including will;

phrases.he: ועיגול הראשון שבו הוא הרצון ותענוג לכללות כל השתלשלות שבתוכו,
phrases.en: and its first circle is the will and delight for the whole chain within it,

phrases.he: ועיגול זה מקיף כללי לאבי''ע כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: and this circle is a general *makif* (encompassing light) for *ABYA*, as mentioned above.

blocks.text: **But in the *ratzon kadum* … which is still within Himself**: the *ratzon kadum* is really still inside of Himself; it has not gone to the outside yet. Therefore it comes in the way of circles, **where the uppermost of all is the hiddenness of this all-including will**, and its first circle is the general *makif* of *ABYA*.

phrases.he: וראשית הקו הוא בחינת המשכה היולית
phrases.en: And the beginning of the *Kav* is a *hiyuli* drawing-down,

phrases.he: כמו קו קצר המתצמצם מעילה לעלול,
phrases.en: like a short line contracted from cause to effect,

phrases.he: כמו מן הרצון לחכמה
phrases.en: as from the will to *chachma*,

phrases.he: וכהאי גוונא
phrases.en: and the like:

phrases.he: כך מבחינת הרשימו הנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: so from the *reshimu* mentioned above

phrases.he: נמשך קו בצמצום גדול מאד
phrases.en: a line is drawn, in a very great contraction.

phrases.he: דהגם שהרשימו הוא בא בהגבלה כנזכר לעיל,
phrases.en: For although the *reshimu* comes in limitation, as mentioned above,

phrases.he: אבל הוא מבחינת עולם האין סוף על כל פנים,
phrases.en: it is still of the world of the *Ein Sof*, at any rate,

phrases.he: רק שהוא בחינת האחרונה שנעשה בקיצור כו'
phrases.en: only it is the last level, made in shortened form;

phrases.he: מה שאין כן להיות רצון קדום שהוא בא לכלל השפעה חוץ מעולם האין סוף
phrases.en: whereas for the *ratzon kadum* to be, which comes to the point of flowing outside the world of the *Ein Sof*,

phrases.he: רק שהוא היולי כולל הכל כו'
phrases.en: only it is a *hiyuli* that includes everything;

phrases.he: על כן נמשך דרך קו קצר כו'
phrases.en: therefore it is drawn by way of a short line,

phrases.he: ודי למבין
phrases.en: and this suffices for one who understands.

blocks.text: **as from the will to *chachma***: from the will to *chachma* only a little thing goes through; not the whole thing goes through. **so from the *reshimu* … a line is drawn, in a very great contraction.**

The *reshimu* is a limitation only in regard to the *Ein Sof*; in regard to what comes after it, it is itself *Ein Sof*. So even though you say that the *reshimu* is nothing, to come down to the *ratzon kadum* you have to make a *tzimtzum* even from that. That is why it is only **by way of a short line**.

phrases.he: (והוא מה שכתוב בעץ חיים דכל עיקר הארת הקו אינו רק להיות בחינת מעלה ומטה
phrases.en: (And this is what is written in *Etz Chaim*, that the whole point of the shining of the *Kav* is only that there be up and down,

phrases.he: כמו ביו''ד עגולים עד סוף מעשה כו'
phrases.en: as in the ten circles, down to the end of the deed;

phrases.he: מה שאין כן בעולם האין סוף אין שם אפילו בחינת מעלה ומטה,
phrases.en: whereas in the world of the *Ein Sof* there is not even up and down,

phrases.he: רק אחדות פשוט בתכלית כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: only utterly simple unity, as mentioned above;

phrases.he: וגם ששיער בעצמו מה שעתיד כו'
phrases.en: and even though He gauged in Himself what would be,

phrases.he: הכל הוא בעצמותו ממש שהוא בבחינת אין סוף ממש
phrases.en: it is all in His very Essence, which is *Ein Sof* *mamash*.

blocks.text: The whole thing of the *Kav* is only to have up and down: to make ten circles, one above the other, down to the end of the deed, to have an order of wills. **whereas in the world of the *Ein Sof***, meaning including the *reshimu*, **there is not even up and down**: no up and down between *chachma* and *bina*, or between *middos* and *sechel*. It is all one thing.

blocks.title: Knowing a man's taste
blocks.text: **it is all in His very Essence**: it is not an actual thing separate from the *Atzmus*. That He gauged in Himself what would be is like a taste: from a person's taste you can tell what he would like, but there is nothing actually there other than just the person. It does not mean there is an actual separate will.

phrases.he: ולזה אמר בעץ חיים דגם בבחינת מלכות דאין סוף אין רשאים לדבר כו'
phrases.en: That is why *Etz Chaim* says that even of *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof* one may not speak;

phrases.he: רק בבחינת הקו ובחינת אדם קדמון כו'
phrases.en: only of the *Kav* and *Adam Kadmon*,

phrases.he: שהוא בחינת מקור הראשון לכל ההשתלשלות,
phrases.en: which is the first source of the whole *hishtalshelus* (chain of descent),

phrases.he: יוכל לבא בהשגה בריבוי ההשתלשלות עד עשר ספירות שבאצילות בבי''ע כו'
phrases.en: can one come to grasp, in the many steps of the chain, down to the ten sefiros of *Atzilus* in *Beriya, Yetzira and Asiya*,

phrases.he: מאחר שנקרא בשם עילת כל העילות כו' או קדמון כו'
phrases.en: since it is called by the name "Cause of all causes" or *Kadmon*.

blocks.text: Even of *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof* you are still not allowed to talk. Why? Because there is nothing to talk about. There is not really a separate thing that you can actually talk about.

You are allowed only from the *Kav*, from *Adam Kadmon*. Really, even the beginning of the *Kav* you should not talk about, because it is *stima d'chol stimin*, which no thought grasps at all. So *Adam Kadmon* is really where you are allowed to start talking. There you can come to grasp it with all kinds of analogies, down to the ten sefiros of *Atzilus* and how they are in *Beriya, Yetzira and Asiya*, and all the way down to how they are in us. *Kadmon* here means *Adam Kadmon*, not the *Kadmon* from before the *tzimtzum*.

phrases.he: אבל בעצמות אור אין סוף לית מחשבה תפיסא ביה,
phrases.en: But in the Essence of the *Or Ein Sof*, "no thought grasps Him,"

phrases.he: אפילו מחשבה הקדומה הנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: not even the primordial thought mentioned above,

phrases.he: להיות כי העולם האין סוף נבדל בערך ונקרא קדוש לגמרי
phrases.en: because the world of the *Ein Sof* is separate in value and is called utterly holy

phrases.he: מצד הצמצום הנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: because of the *tzimtzum* mentioned above.

phrases.he: ובחינת רצון קדום הנזכר לעיל נקרא שמו הגדול,
phrases.en: And the *ratzon kadum* mentioned above is called His great Name:

phrases.he: שמו גימטריא רצון,
phrases.en: *shemo* (His Name) has the numerical value of *ratzon*;

phrases.he: והוא ענין יהא שמיה רבה מברך כו'
phrases.en: and this is "May His great Name be blessed."

blocks.text: There, in the Essence of the *Or Ein Sof*, even the *machshava kduma* cannot grasp. The hidden *Ein Sof* has totally nothing to do with what is after the *tzimtzum*.

**"May His great Name be blessed"**: the great Name means that the upper, general will should come down to here; that the original *machshava kduma*, which is for the end of the deed of the seventh millennium, should come down to here: that *Moshiach* should come.

phrases.he: (וכידוע דבחינת אדם קדמון נקרא אדם דבריאה כו'
phrases.en: (As is known, *Adam Kadmon* is called the man of creation,

phrases.he: וכמו שיתבאר
phrases.en: as will be explained;

phrases.he: מה שאין כן בעצמות אור אין סוף נאמר כי לא אדם הוא כו'
phrases.en: whereas of the Essence of the *Or Ein Sof* it is said, "For He is not a man";

phrases.he: וכידוע בכונות דנשמת כל חי, שהוא בחינת אדם קדמון כו'
phrases.en: and as is known in the *kavanos* of *Nishmas kol chai*, that it is *Adam Kadmon*, etc.;

phrases.he: ודי למבין):
phrases.en: and this suffices for one who understands.)

blocks.text: Of the Essence of the *Or Ein Sof* it says He is not a man. *Adam Kadmon* is called a man: that is already a shape of a man. But in the Essence of the *Or Ein Sof* there is no shape at all. "And that was chapter 17."

After the chapter is finished he adds: that sometimes he wants something and sometimes he does not; that is the will for himself, and it is what causes the will for a will. He wants to be himself and to have all the things he needs, so it makes a will to have a will for anything he needs in order to be himself.
blocks.outOfPlace: Said after the chapter is read to the end ("And that was chapter 17"), on the ratzon kadum of the whole chapter.

blocks.text: That is why the *ratzon kadum* is not a new creation. It was always there, and it is part of the true *ayin* (nothing). That it is *ayin* does not mean it is a nothing: if it is a nothing, how did it make the something? It means it is not a something by itself. The *ratzon kadum* is literally part of Him; it is not a separate entity, not a something.
blocks.outOfPlace: Said after the chapter is read to the end, on the ratzon kadum of the whole chapter.

reviewQuestions.question: How does the ratzon kadum differ from the ratzon hapashut, and in what way is it still the same thing?
How can the ratzon kadum hold every detail when it is only a will for Himself? What do the bird's house and the king's suit show?
Why did the end of the deed come up first in the primordial thought?
What are Atika d'Atikin, Atika Stima'a and Atika Kadisha, and where is the will revealed?
In the circles, what are chachma and bina to the will, and why does the effect never reach its cause?
Why is the order reversed in yosher, so that the deed is the uppermost and the will the innermost?
